problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-3,0),(1,5),(2,-2).$  Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(-2,2)$
- $(0,3)$
- $(-1,-5)$
worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by the same angle. It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-{180}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(3,0),(-1,-5),(-2,2).$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."
